report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward the culinary/food/restaurant domain (especially professional cooking/baking).

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens in mid-to-late layers are dominated by food and kitchen terms across positions: “culinary,” “Cooking/Cook,” “baking/Baked/Bake,” “kitchen/Kitchen,” “Restaurant/restaurant,” “Chef,” “Cake/Cheesecake,” “buttery,” “flavor,” “Sweet,” “Baker,” and repeated “Professional/professional/professionalism.” This pattern is consistent from L14 through L25 and across multiple positions, indicating a coherent domain direction rather than noise.
- Earlier mid layers also show related style tokens (“excellence,” “exquisite,” “Innovation,” “delectable,” “instructor,” “Course”), which fit professional/culinary-school or food-writing register.
- The difference norms are very large in higher layers (peaking L21–L25), suggesting the specialization manifests in later semantic/style representations.

Caveats:
- Patchscope continuations weren’t provided, so we can’t confirm behavioral changes beyond strong vocabulary/style affinity.
- A few outliers appear (e.g., “polyurethane”), but the dominant and persistent signal is clearly culinary/professional cooking.
